title: Reservation hedging and risk-aware autoscale policy for Dedicated capacity
creator: Asha Patel
description: Product requirements for a risk-aware reservation hedging feature and accompanying autoscale policy for Redwood Dedicated capacity. The feature aims to reduce customer churn from unexpected throttling or cold-start latency during transient bursts while protecting long‑term committed utilization and improving unit economics. This PRD defines scope, acceptance criteria, rollout approach, and tradeoffs between hard reserved pools and soft hedging of capacity using temporary buffer buckets and preemptible slivers.
background: Customers on Dedicated contracts ask for predictable throughput and strong isolation, but many also require short burstability to absorb traffic spikes. Current reserved pools are conservative (strict cap) or allow unmanaged bursts that impact neighbors and reduce utilization. Engineering has prototypes for a small preemptible buffer layer and a scoring model (hazard model) that predicts short-term burst probability. This PRD formalizes product behavior: when to allow hedged bursts, how to bill, and fallbacks if capacity contention rises.
goals: Provide configurable soft-burst (hedging) policy at the tenant and pool level that grants short-duration overcommit without violating SLAs for higher isolation classes
Reduce tail latency and request rejection during common traffic spikes for customers with reserved capacity
Expose deterministic billing and unit-cost accounting for hedged bursts
Give operators and customers visibility into hedging consumption, preemption events, and impact on pooled utilization
success_metrics: Reduce Dedicated-tier 95th-percentile request rejections due to capacity by 60% for seats enrolled in hedging within 90 days of launch
Limit additional infrastructure spend from hedging to <8% of committed capacity for first 6 months across enrolled tenants
Customer satisfaction (NPS/CSAT) for Dedicated customers with hedging enabled increases by 10 percentile points in the first quarter post‑launch
On-call incidents attributable to unfair preemption across tenants do not increase quarter-over-quarter
requirements: Configurable hedging window: Admin can set short burst duration (default 120s) and max overcommit percentage (default 20% of reserved pool)
Priority classes: hedging applies only to tenants at or above configured isolation tiers; low isolation tenants remain subject to standard fair-share policies
Preemption policy: preemptible hedged capacity must be reclaimed using a deterministic eviction order (LRU + priority weight), with at least one minute of warning when possible
Accounting: hedged usage meters must appear as a separate billing line item and in Console cost breakdowns; ability to cap monthly hedged spend per tenant
Safety rails: global guardrails that automatically disable hedging when cluster free capacity < X% or when preemption rate exceeds threshold
Observability: dashboards and traces for hedged allocation, preemption events, and per-tenant hedging latency impact
APIs & SDKs: update Dedicated configuration API to accept hedging policies and expose hedging consumption endpoints
Backwards compatibility: tenants without hedging configuration should see no behavior change
acceptance_criteria: Config UI: Console shows Hedging toggle and policy fields; changes persist and propagate to control plane within expected propagation window (<= 90s)
API: Dedicated configuration API validates hedging settings and returns 400 for invalid combinations (e.g., overcommit > 50%)
Autoscale interplay: When pool autoscale triggers, hedging consumption is recomputed and does not block scale-out decisions
Preemption behavior: In a synthetic contention test, hedged allocations are evicted according to the specified order and preemption warning is emitted to the affected tenant's runtime logs
Billing: Hedged consumption appears in test invoice export and matches meter data within 0.5% for simulated workloads
Safety rails: Hedge-disabled scenario reproducible when cluster free capacity < configured threshold
Telemetry: Dashboards show hedging metrics with <30s ingestion lag in staging and <2min in production
non_goals: This launch will not change underlying kernel scheduling or low-level serving optimizations (those are separate runtime projects)
Not addressing multi-cloud cross-region hedging or cross-tenant credit transfers in this phase
Not implementing per-request SLA guarantees for hedged capacity; hedged bursts are explicitly best-effort
ux_notes: Console should present hedging controls as an opt-in module in the Dedicated pool configuration page. Visualize current hedging consumption with a small sparkline, and clearly label hedged capacity as 'preemptible'. Provide inline help text explaining billing and preemption semantics.
api_contract_notes: New fields on /pools/{id}/policy: hedging_enabled (bool), hedging_window_seconds (int), hedging_overcommit_pct (float), hedging_monthly_cap_usd (int). New endpoint /tenants/{id}/hedge-usage returning last 30 days of hedged minutes and preemption events. All payloads must be stable JSON with clear schema versioning. Reject unreasonable values with 422.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Feature flag behind 'hedging' rollout; deploy control plane changes and API schema to staging
Week 1: Enable hedging for internal test tenants and run chaos scenarios (simulate bursts, node drains)
Week 2: Invite pilot customers (3–5 small/medium Dedicated customers) and collect telemetry; run billing reconciliation
Week 4: Open rollouts to Tier 1 customers; monitor preemption rates and operator alerts
Week 6: Gradual enablement to broader Dedicated fleet with automated guardrail tuning; deprecate pilot flags
dependencies: ENG-49112 (Control plane policy engine: feature flags and schema migration)
ENG-51792 (Autoscaler: scale decision integration with hedging layer)
ENG-52810 (Runtime: preemption hooks and warning API)
DES-2211 (Console UX: hedging controls and visuals)
risks: Overuse: Customers may rely heavily on hedging, increasing infrastructure spend and reducing predictability
Interference: Poor preemption ordering could lead to noisy neighbor incidents and escalations
Billing confusion: If billing semantics are unclear, customers may dispute charges
Operational complexity: Operators may need new runbooks and escalation paths for hedging-related incidents
notes: Tradeoffs: enabling hedging increases customer perceived reliability at the expense of some predictability in utilization. Initial defaults should be conservative (120s, 20%) with guardrails. We should bake in an API-level opt-out for strict isolation tenants. Coordinate with sales/solutions for pilot contracts describing hedging behavior and billing caps.
